chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The young boy is not penalised by the hadd punishment when he falls upon a woman, and the man is penalised by the hadd punishment when he falls upon the young girl.

key_terms.الصَّبِيَّة: The young girl/minor female who has not yet reached puberty
key_terms.الصَّبِيّ: The young boy/minor male who has not yet reached puberty (bulugh)
key_terms.حَدّ: Hadd (pl. hudud) — the fixed, divinely prescribed punishment for specific offenses in Islamic law
key_terms.وَقَعَ عَلَى: Euphemism for sexual intercourse in classical Arabic fiqh texts

ai.seo_question: Does a minor boy incur hadd punishment for zina in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a foundational principle of Islamic criminal jurisprudence: the hadd punishment for illicit sexual intercourse (zina) does not apply to a minor (sabiyy), even if he initiates the act with an adult woman. Conversely, an adult man who commits zina with an underage girl does incur the full hadd penalty. This ruling reflects the classical fiqh principle that legal accountability (taklif) requires maturity (bulugh), such that a minor cannot be held to the same legal penalties as a legally responsible adult. The ruling was addressed to Imam al-Sadiq's circle of jurist-students who were systematically learning the rulings of Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The young boy would not be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd)) if he were to fall upon a woman, and the man would be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd)) when he falls upon the young child’.
